Customs Act 1969: The Act provides the enabling authority under Section 219, read with Item 17 of the Third Schedule, for the National Board of Revenue to frame new baggage rules.
National Board of Revenue: The board is empowered by the Customs Act 1969 to enact procedural rules governing the import of baggage by passengers.
Passenger (Non-Tourist) Baggage (Import): These previous rules are formally repealed and replaced by the newly enacted baggage regulations.
Third Schedule: Item 17 of this schedule provides the specific legal basis, when read with Section 219 of the Customs Act, for the issuance of the current baggage rules.
S.R.O. 172-AIN/2012: This statutory regulatory order establishes the new baggage rules for non-tourist passengers following the repeal of the previous 2011 regulations.

Passenger Baggage Allowance: Passengers arriving by air or water who are at least twelve years old may import personal hand baggage, cabin baggage, and checked baggage up to a specified weight limit free of all duties and taxes.
A duty-free allowance for additional personal items such as clothing, books, and study materials is granted to passengers, subject to specific weight limits beyond the standard baggage allowance.
Passengers under twelve years of age are entitled to a specific weight allowance for personal baggage brought in cartons, bags, or sacks, free of duties and taxes.
Passengers may import professional tools or equipment that are portable and intended for use in their occupation without the payment of duties and taxes.
The import of gold or silver jewelry is permitted duty-free up to specified weight limits, provided the number of individual pieces of each type does not exceed a defined count.
Passengers may import gold or silver bars or ingots upon the payment of applicable duties and taxes, subject to established weight thresholds.
Unaccompanied Baggage: Baggage not accompanying a passenger may be cleared duty-free provided a declaration is submitted in the prescribed format as stipulated in the relevant schedule.
The clearance of unaccompanied baggage requires the passenger to submit a copy of the declaration form to the appropriate customs officer.
Customs: Customs officers are responsible for receiving the baggage declaration forms submitted by passengers for the clearance of unaccompanied baggage.
Duty-Free Baggage Items: Foreign passport holders are permitted to import a specified quantity of alcoholic beverages, such as spirit or beer, free of all duties and taxes.
Passenger Baggage Purchase Form: Passengers may purchase specific goods mentioned in the prescribed schedules from designated sales centers within a set number of working days after their arrival, provided they document the purchase in the required declaration form.

Passenger Baggage Allowance: Passengers arriving via land routes are permitted to import baggage up to a defined maximum value without the obligation to pay any customs duties or taxes. This allowance is applicable regardless of the duration the passenger spent abroad.

Passenger Baggage Allowance: Passengers who are sick, disabled, or elderly are granted the privilege to import their medical equipment and wheelchairs free of all duties and taxes.
This exemption applies to such essential mobility and medical items regardless of the mode of transport, including air, water, or land routes.

Airline Crew Baggage Allowance: Bangladeshi crew or officials working for airlines, whether Bangladeshi or foreign-operated, are permitted to import baggage up to a specified maximum value free of all duties and taxes upon returning from professional duties abroad.
Seafarer Baggage Allowance: Bangladeshi seafarers or officials arriving from foreign seaports are entitled to import baggage up to a defined maximum value free of all duties and taxes.
Upon signing off, seafarers or officials are permitted to import additional baggage up to a higher maximum value, provided that all applicable duties and taxes are paid.
Transport Crew Baggage Allowance: Drivers and supervisors of passenger buses arriving from abroad are exempt from duties and taxes on personal clothing, bedding, and cooked food items.
These individuals may also import personal and household goods up to a specified maximum value free of all duties and taxes.

Customs: Customs officials are responsible for the random selection and examination of baggage passing through the Green Channel.
Customs officials maintain the discretionary power to inspect any passenger's baggage at the Green Channel if they have reasonable grounds for suspicion.

Baggage Rules: This schedule provides the list of items subject to duty and taxes under the passenger baggage regulations.
It sets out specific thresholds and duty conditions for goods imported as baggage that are not for personal or household use, exceed quantity limits, or are imported in commercial quantities.
Television: Televisions of various display technologies like Plasma, LCD, and LED are subject to graded duty payments based on their screen size categories.
Home Theatre System: Home theatre systems or music centers exceeding a specific speaker count are subject to a fixed rate of duty.
Refrigerator: Refrigerators and deep freezers imported as baggage are liable for a specific fixed amount of duty.
Air Conditioner: Air coolers and air conditioners are categorized by type and capacity, with distinct duty rates applied to each category.
Dish Antenna: The import of a dish antenna under baggage rules requires the payment of a specified amount of duty.
Gold Bar: Gold bars or ingots up to a maximum weight limit are permitted for import as baggage subject to a specific duty rate per unit of weight.
Silver Bar: Silver bars or ingots up to a maximum weight limit are allowed as baggage imports upon payment of a defined duty rate per unit of weight.
Professional Equipment: Professional cameras and camcorders, including HD and Beta cam units, are subject to a fixed duty payment when imported as baggage.
Airgun: The import of airguns or air rifles as baggage is subject to a fixed duty and requires prior approval from the Ministry of Commerce.
Chandelier: Chandeliers imported as baggage are subject to duty calculated on a per-point basis.
Carpet: Carpets up to a specified total area are permitted for import under baggage rules upon payment of duty calculated per square meter.
Household Appliance: Appliances such as dishwashers, washing machines, and cloth dryers are subject to a fixed duty amount when imported as baggage.
